name: Albany County
intro: Albany County sits at the center of the Capital Region, home to the state capital and its suburbs along the Hudson. The Albany County Department for Aging helps residents 60 and older with caregiver support, legal help, NY Connects referrals, adult day programs and in-home check-ins. Its ride partner is ACCESS Transit Services, a CDTA service that books trips for older residents with no other way to reach medical visits, pharmacies, grocery stores and meal sites.

The Allegany County Office for the Aging in Belmont offers HIICAP health insurance counseling, meals, in-home services, caregiver support and legal help. Volunteer drivers give rides to residents 60 and older, with at least two days' notice.

name: Brooklyn (Kings County)
intro: Brooklyn sits across the East River from Manhattan, and older Brooklynites get help through NYC Aging. The agency's older adult centers serve daily meals, and it also offers caregiver help and job help for people who want to keep working. Call Aging Connect at 212-AGING-NYC (212-244-6469) or 311 to ask about Pop-Up Produce and other programs near you.

name: Broome County

The Broome County Office for Aging offers Meals on Wheels, in-home services, caregiver support, NY Connects and free legal help for eligible residents 60 and older. Its Office for Aging Mini-bus takes riders 60 and up around the urban parts of the county on weekdays for a $2.00 contribution with an Office for Aging ID card.

name: The Bronx (Bronx County)
intro: The Bronx sits just north of Manhattan, and older adults here get help through NYC Aging. The agency's older adult centers serve daily meals, and it also offers caregiver help, job help and support for older adults facing elder abuse or crime. Call Aging Connect at 212-AGING-NYC (212-244-6469) or dial 311 to find a center or a service near you.

name: Tioga County
intro: Tioga County lies along the Susquehanna River on the Pennsylvania line, with the village of Owego as its county seat. Aging services here run through Tioga Opportunities, Inc., which offers home delivered meals, congregate dining, in-home care, respite for caregivers and Medicare counseling. For rides, the county lists Getthere, a mobility management service focused on older adults in rural areas that helps people find and plan trips.

name: Tompkins County
intro: Tompkins County sits at the southern end of Cayuga Lake, with the city of Ithaca as its county seat. The Tompkins County Office for the Aging offers NY Connects, HIICAP Medicare counseling, EISEP in-home services, HEAP help, yard work and snow shoveling help, and minor home safety repairs. For rides, Gadabout is a volunteer transportation service for older and disabled Tompkins County residents.

name: Ulster County
intro: Ulster County runs from the west bank of the Hudson into the Catskill and Shawangunk mountains. The Office for the Aging in Kingston offers HIICAP Medicare counseling, NY Connects, senior meals and the Neighbor to Neighbor program, where volunteer drivers take older residents to doctor visits. Registered seniors 60 and older also get one free round trip a week for shopping and up to two medical trips a week.

name: Warren County
intro: Warren County covers Lake George and the southeastern Adirondacks, with Glens Falls and Queensbury as its population center. One shared office, the Warren/Hamilton Counties Office for the Aging, serves both Warren and Hamilton counties from the Human Services Building in Lake George. It offers volunteer rides to medical appointments and scheduled town transportation in places like Lake George and Lake Luzerne.

name: Washington County
intro: Washington County is a long, rural county between the upper Hudson and the Vermont border, with its county offices in Fort Edward. The Washington County Office for Aging and Disability Resource Center works to help older residents stay as independent as possible for as long as possible, and it is home to NY Connects for free, unbiased long term care information. The office uses the Blooming Health platform to reach the people it serves by voice, text and email in 70 languages.

name: Wayne County
intro: Wayne County runs along the Lake Ontario shore between Rochester and Syracuse, with the Erie Canal passing through Palmyra, Newark and Lyons. Services for older adults come from the Wayne County Department of Aging and Youth in Lyons, which offers Medicare insurance help, NY Connects, caregiver services and Lunch Club 60 meal sites. RTS Wayne runs the public bus in the county.

name: Westchester County
intro: Westchester County sits just north of the Bronx, between the Hudson River and Long Island Sound. Its Department of Senior Programs and Services, based in Mount Vernon, runs the Livable Communities Initiative to help people stay in their homes, plus caregiver coaching and in-home services. For people who cannot ride regular buses, Bee-Line ParaTransit offers shared curb to curb rides for a $5 fare.

name: Wyoming County
intro: Wyoming County is a rural county of farms and small villages south of Batavia, sharing Letchworth State Park with Livingston County. The Wyoming County Office for the Aging in Warsaw helps with caregiver support, home delivered meals, respite, housing and benefit programs such as EPIC, Medicare and HEAP. RTS Wyoming runs the county's public transit.

name: Yates County
intro: Yates County is a small rural county wrapped around Keuka Lake, with Seneca Lake on its eastern edge. The Yates County Area Agency on Aging works out of the County Office Building on Liberty Street in Penn Yan, and it is the county office NYSOFA lists for older adults and caregivers. Public transit in the county has been changing, so call the agency to ask what rides are available now.
